rule: Translate the multicolour fragments, without rotating them, so they tile one rectangle whose outer border is entirely the dominant frame colour. The rectangle's corner sits on the empty cell of the 3-cell L marker's 2x2 box and extends away from the marker. Output the background with only that rectangle; the marker and the original fragments are erased.
scope: Translate connected multicolour fragments into a solid framed rectangle anchored at the missing cell of a three-cell L marker. Random rectangles have sides 4..24, short side at most 12 and area at most 240; three to ten irregular connected pieces. All anchor corners, exact canvas dimensions and partial background/marker palette controls are supported.

authored_scope:
Random mode builds a latent framed rectangle. Each side is 4..18, the short side is at most 12 and the area is at most 180; small sizes are favoured. The interior gets 1..4 non-touching accent shapes (rings, blocks with optional holes, bars) in 1..3 accent colours. The rectangle is cut into 3..10 compact 4-connected pieces of at least 3 cells each. Any of the four anchor corners is possible, the grid is 10..30 per side, and bg, marker, frame and accent colours are all random and distinct. Pieces are scattered without touching each other or the marker. The longer-side range up to 18 is a synthetic extension; test 1 shows a 22x10 rectangle, so long thin rectangles are within the task domain. Explicit mode reproduces fixtures from rectangle contents, a label map and offsets.

Not supported: rotated or reflected fragments, fragments in the frame colour only that are ambiguous in shape, rectangles longer than 18 in random mode, and more than 10 pieces in random mode. Partial explicit parameters such as rect_top without rect_rows are rejected rather than silently ignored.
authored_constraints: The marker colour differs from the background and from every fragment colour, and is the only colour with exactly 3 cells.
No fragment colour other than the marker has a count of exactly 3.
The frame colour is strictly the most frequent fragment colour.
The background is strictly the most frequent input colour: grid area is at least 3*area+40.
The rectangle's border is entirely frame colour; accents lie strictly in the interior and do not touch each other.
Pieces are 4-connected with at least 3 cells each; pieces with identical coloured shapes are rejected.
No two pieces touch, even diagonally, and no piece touches the marker.
Rectangle and marker fit in the grid; the marker is in-bounds at the chosen corner.

An exhaustive framed translation-tiling search over every area factorisation that fits at the anchor finds only tilings equal to the latent picture. Scenes that exhaust the 60000-node budget are rejected.
Retry loops are bounded at 500 scene attempts and 300 placements per piece.
